info.name: Pawfront Backend API
info.description:
Complete API testing suite for the Pawfront provider-facing backend.

**Setup**
1. Set the `baseUrl` collection variable (default `https://localhost:5001`).
2. Get a Firebase ID token (see CLAUDE.md `Get a fresh Firebase ID token`) and set `firebaseToken`.
3. Run requests roughly in folder order. Several requests have test scripts that auto-populate ids (`providerAuthIdentityId`, `providerId`, `otpId`, `eventId`, `bookingId`, plus the per-service-type `serviceId*` vars).

**Notes**
- Every endpoint requires the `FirebaseUser` policy → `Authorization: Bearer {{firebaseToken}}`.
- All responses follow the `ApiResponse<T>` envelope: `{ success, data, error }`.
- A provider can register only ONE service category. Pick one of the five service folders and stick to it for a given `providerId`.
- **Per-service flow:** after a provider saves an offering, the server upserts a row in `Provider.ProviderServices` for each sub-offering present (e.g. PetSitter with DayCare + NightStay = two ServiceIds). Closures, bookings, and slot queries are all scoped by `ServiceId`. **Run `3z. Provider Services Catalog → GET /services` after the offering save** — its test script populates `serviceId`, `serviceIdDayCare`, `serviceIdNightStay`, `serviceIdGrooming`, `serviceIdTraining`, `serviceIdVet` for use in the later folders.
- Image-upload requests use multipart with field name `file`.

variable.description: A multi-night booking id (created on the parent host) for the provider-side night-stay management endpoints.
A pet id (from GET /pet-parents/{petParentId}/details pets[] or a booking's petDetails) for the provider-facing pet lookup.
Catch-all: first active ServiceId returned by GET /services. Use when you only care about one service (single-offering categories).
PetSitter DayCare ServiceId. Populated by GET /services if the provider offers DayCare.
PetSitter NightStay ServiceId. Populated by GET /services if the provider offers NightStay.

request.description: Returns the persisted personal information for this provider — name, gender, mobile, date of birth, mobile-verified timestamp, onboarding status, isActive, created/updated timestamps. Returns 404 ProviderProfileNotFound when the row is missing.

item.name: PATCH provider profile (edit name / gender / DOB)

request.description: Edits the provider's personal details (the app's "Edit Profile" screen): firstName, lastName, gender, dateOfBirth. Returns the same shape as GET profile, so the client can rebind straight from the response. Deliberately NOT editable here: mobileCountryCode / mobileNumber (a change must go back through OTP verification, and the pair is UNIQUE), bannerImageUrl (own endpoint), onboardingStatus / isActive (own flows). gender ∈ { Male, Female, NonBinary, Other, PreferNotToSay }. 404 ProviderProfileNotFound; 409 ProviderAccountDeleted (the account was deleted — editing would undo the anonymisation); 400 UnsupportedGender | InvalidRequest.

Resolves the caller's Firebase uid → { providerAuthIdentityId, providerId?, hasProfile, onboardingStatus?, isActive? }. Used by mobile after reinstall to recover the ProviderId. Re-captures providerAuthIdentityId / providerId.

The app's "Delete account" action. IRREVERSIBLE — it disables the account you are signed in as. This is an ANONYMISE + DISABLE, not a row delete: the ProviderId stays valid so nothing that references it loses meaning.

RETAINED untouched: single-day and night-stay bookings with all their audit / evidence / OTP / modification / prescription children, the events you organised plus their ticket bookings, and the Booking.BookingPayments ledger. Deleting those would destroy the pet parents' history too, since their bookings reference you.

ANONYMISED: the Providers row — name becomes "Deleted Provider", gender/DOB/mobile are replaced, banner + mobileVerifiedAtUtc cleared, IsActive → 0 and IsDeleted → 1. IsActive = 0 blocks new bookings (409 ProviderInactive); IsDeleted = 1 is permanent and also blocks reactivation and profile edits (409 ProviderAccountDeleted). The Firebase auth identity is scrubbed too, which severs the login AND frees the real Firebase uid + phone number — so you can sign up again and get a brand-new ProviderId.

DELETED: operational config + media only — device tokens, mobile OTPs, gallery photos, per-service banners, weekly availability, closures, cancellation policy, payout methods, service registration. Bookable services are DEACTIVATED (their rows must stay: bookings FK to ServiceId). The provider's Cosmos offering document (the public listing) is removed, so you drop out of parent-facing discovery, and GET /providers/{providerId} then returns 404 ProviderNotRegistered.

Idempotent: a second call returns the original deletedAtUtc with wasAlreadyDeleted = true. Response carries retained* counts so you can confirm history survived.

The caller's ProviderId is taken from the JWT and must match the route → 403 Forbidden otherwise. 404 ProviderProfileNotFound when the provider row is missing.

item.name: 3z. Provider Services Catalog (run after offering save)
item.description: Returns the SQL-backed catalog of services the provider currently offers. Rows are upserted automatically by the offering POSTs (one row per sub-offering present — e.g. PetSitter with DayCare + NightStay = two rows). The test script on `GET /services` populates per-ServiceType collection variables (`serviceIdDayCare`, `serviceIdNightStay`, `serviceIdGrooming`, `serviceIdTraining`, `serviceIdVet`) plus the generic `serviceId` (first active row) for use in the Availability / Closures / Bookings folders below.

request.description: Includes services that were deactivated (the provider removed the matching sub-offering on a later save). Historical closures / bookings can still reference these ServiceIds, so the row is kept.

Uploads/replaces the wide banner image for one bookable service (ServiceId). Distinct from the offering's discovery/profile image. <=5 MB, JPEG/PNG/WebP. The ServiceId must belong to the provider and be active (else 400 InvalidServiceId). Returns { serviceId, providerId, bannerImageUrl, createdAtUtc, updatedAtUtc }. Run after `GET /services` so `{{serviceId}}` is populated.
Reads the banner for a service. 404 ServiceBannerNotFound when none is set (or the service isn't this provider's).

item.name: 4b. Provider Active Status (master switch)
item.description: Single master Active/Inactive switch above the per-service catalog. When Inactive, every NEW booking is rejected with 409 ProviderInactive. Always returns 200 with a discriminated payload: `status: "Updated"` (flag flipped) or `status: "BookingsExist"` (deactivation blocked — `conflictingBookings` lists future confirmed bookings; there is NO force override).

request.description: On deactivation the server checks for future confirmed bookings. If any exist it returns `status: "BookingsExist"` (flag NOT flipped) with the conflict list. Otherwise `status: "Updated"`.
Activation is always applied immediately (no conflict check). Returns `status: "Updated"`.

item.name: 4c. Provider Photos (gallery)
item.description: General provider photo gallery (separate from the per-service profile/service images). One row per upload.

request.description: multipart/form-data — attach a `file` (≤3 MB, JPEG/PNG/WebP). Captures `providerPhotoId`. 404 ProviderNotFound; 400 InvalidFile/ImageTooLarge/UnsupportedImageFormat.
Lists the provider's gallery photos, oldest-first ([] when none).
Removes one photo (scoped by ProviderId + PhotoId) + best-effort blob delete. 404 ProviderPhotoNotFound.

Slots are computed per-service: capacity, duration rule, partial-day closures, and overlap-with-existing-bookings are all scoped by `serviceId`. Each returned slot carries `remainingCapacity` (capacity minus active bookings overlapping the window); fully-booked windows are returned with `remainingCapacity: 0` so the client can render them as unavailable. For single-offering categories (PetGroomer/PetTrainer/Vet) use `{{serviceId}}` instead of `{{serviceIdDayCare}}`.

NightStay is DATE-granular: capacity is per night, not per time window. The response fills `nights` (one entry per night in date..endDate, max 31: `{ date, activeBookings, remainingCapacity, isClosed, isAvailable }`) and leaves `slots` empty; `durationHours`/`granularityMinutes` are ignored. A night is unavailable when a full-day closure covers it or active stays (CheckInDate <= night < CheckOutDate) have used every capacity unit. `endDate` defaults to `date` (single night).

item.name: 5b. Provider Closures (sick leave / vacation) — PER-SERVICE
item.description: Closures are scoped by `ServiceId`. A single POST can close ONE or MANY services at the same time by passing an array of `serviceIds`; the server inserts one closure row per service in a single transaction (all-or-nothing). A closure on DayCare does NOT block NightStay slots/bookings, and vice versa.

item.name: POST close ONE service — DayCare full day

exec: console.warn('Closure batch rejected — bookings exist on one or more services:', json.data.conflictingBookings);

body.raw:
{
  "serviceIds": ["{{serviceIdDayCare}}"],
  "startDate": "2026-06-01",
  "endDate": "2026-06-01",
  "startTime": null,
  "endTime": null,
  "reason": "Sick leave (DayCare only — NightStay remains open)"
}

request.description:
Closes DayCare for the whole day on 2026-06-01. NightStay bookings on the same day are unaffected.

**Response shape (always 200 + success=true):**
- `data.status = "Created"` → `data.closures` is populated (one entry per requested ServiceId).
- `data.status = "BookingsExist"` → no closures were created. `data.conflictingBookings` lists confirmed bookings inside the window across ALL targeted services (each carries its `serviceId`); `data.warningMessage` is the human-readable message. The provider must move/cancel those bookings and retry.

item.name: POST close MULTIPLE services — DayCare + NightStay together (vacation)

request.description: Atomic batch close across two services. Server creates two closure rows (one per ServiceId) in a single transaction. If ANY of the targeted services has a conflicting confirmed booking inside the window, the WHOLE batch is rejected and no rows are inserted.

item.name: POST close single-service provider — generic (PetGroomer / PetTrainer / Vet)

request.description: For categories with only one ServiceType (PetGroomer / PetTrainer / Vet), the generic `{{serviceId}}` collection variable (first active row from `GET /services`) is the easy choice.

item.name: POST close service — partial day (e.g. vet appointment block)

request.description: Partial-day window. StartTime + EndTime must be set together; StartDate must equal EndDate when times are present (multi-day partial windows are rejected with 400 InvalidRequest).

Returns closures whose date range intersects [from, to] across ALL the provider's services. Each row carries `serviceId` so the UI can group them. Both `from` and `to` are optional — omit either for an open-ended side.
Narrow to closures for one specific service.
Reopens a single closure row (one ServiceId). If you closed DayCare + NightStay together as two rows, you must DELETE each closureId to reopen both.

body.raw:
{
  "petParentId": "{{petParentId}}",
  "serviceId": "{{serviceIdDayCare}}",
  "bookingDate": "2026-05-20",
  "startTime": "10:00:00",
  "endTime": "12:00:00",
  "jobNotes": "Gate code is 1234; Bruno is shy around strangers.",
  "locationType": "ProviderLocation"
}

request.description:
`serviceId` is REQUIRED. The server validates that this ServiceId belongs to the provider and is active (else 400 InvalidServiceId). Capacity is checked per-service — DayCare bookings count separately from NightStay bookings, and closures only block if they target the same ServiceId.

`jobNotes` is optional free-text (access instructions, the pet's quirks) — captured here and returned on the booking detail. `locationType` is OPTIONAL on this host ('ParentLocation' | 'ProviderLocation'; 400 UnsupportedLocationType otherwise) — when set, the booking detail resolves the matching address. For PetSitter NightStay use `{{serviceIdNightStay}}`. For single-offering categories (PetGroomer / PetTrainer / Vet) use `{{serviceId}}`.

NightStay on the SAME date as DayCare — both can exist independently. (Note: this example uses a NightStay window that crosses midnight; valid only if the provider's weekly availability covers it. Adjust to your provider's hours.)
Returns the full booking history for this provider when no `date` query param is given.

item.name: GET bookings by provider — filter by date

request.description: Returns only the bookings whose `bookingDate` equals the provided `date` (YYYY-MM-DD). Used by the provider's day-view UI.

Sectioned detail: { bookingDetails, parentDetails, petDetails, providerDetails, paymentDetails, cancellationPolicy, location, startOtp (always null on the provider host — the OTP is parent-only), pendingModification (staged date/time proposal, populated only while a MODIFICATION_REQUEST_BY_* is open), prescription }. `providerDetails` = { providerId, providerName, providerMobileCountryCode, providerMobile, providerGender, providerPhotoUrl (null for now), address, city, zip } — address/city/zip are the provider's registered BUSINESS address (Cosmos service doc), added so the client needn't call GET /providers/{id} just for the address; null when the offering can't be resolved. `parentDetails` also carries the parent's profile address (addressLine, city, zipCode, latitude, longitude — App bookings only). `petDetails` carries the FULL medical snapshot: breed, vaccinationStatus, vaccinationType, vaccinationDose, prescription, sterilizationStatus, medicalHistory, temperament (from the pet's profile; null for Custom walk-ins). `location` = { locationType (ParentLocation | ProviderLocation | null), addressLine, city, zipCode, latitude, longitude } — the parent's address for ParentLocation, the provider's registered business address for ProviderLocation. `bookingDetails.serviceLocation` is populated for App bookings (the offering's service-location) and `jobNotes` carries the booking notes; `cancellationPolicy` is a dedicated section { minimumHoursBeforeCancellation }. `prescription` = { prescriptionText, isPetVaccinated, vaccinations[], nextConsultationDate } — the vet's recorded prescription; NULL until a vet records one (Vet bookings only, via POST .../complete or POST .../prescription).

SNAPSHOTS (2026-07-24): `paymentDetails.pricePerHour`, `cancellationPolicy.minimumHoursBeforeCancellation` and the `location` address are read from values FROZEN onto the booking at creation, so editing your price, cancellation policy, or business address never changes bookings that already exist. Bookings created before this shipped fall back to live resolution. (The `parentDetails` / `providerDetails` CONTACT addresses are deliberately NOT frozen — they always show current contact info.)

Provider sets CONFIRMED | COMPLETED | APPROVAL_NEEDED | PROVIDER_CANCELLED on a booking they're a party to; audited. Actor + id come from the route, never the body. 403 Forbidden (not this provider's booking); 400 BookingStatusNotAllowed; 409 BookingStatusTerminal | BookingStatusUnchanged.
Full status audit trail, oldest-first. 404 if the booking isn't this provider's.

Provider accepts a CREATED booking → CONFIRMED A booking left in CREATED for 24+ hours is automatically EXPIRED (by the background sweeper, or lazily on this call) and can no longer be accepted → 409 BookingExpired.
Provider declines a CREATED booking → PROVIDER_DECLINED (terminal; frees the capacity slot).

Provider taps "Start Job" (no body): the booking moves to START_JOB and the parent's start-OTP is issued (the parent reads it from GET .../bookings/{id} on the parent host). Two gates: today must BE the booking's service date (bookingDate), and the provider must be inside their own weekly working hours (Provider.ProviderWeeklyAvailability for today, UTC). The scheduled start TIME does not gate it. 409 BookingNotOnServiceDate | OutsideWorkingHours | BookingNotStartable.
Provider enters the start-code the parent showed → IN_PROGRESS. 6 wrong attempts cancel the job (409 OtpAttemptsExceeded). 400 InvalidStartOtp; 409 StartOtpExpired | BookingNotStartable.
Provider uploads a job-completion evidence photo (≤3 MB, JPEG/PNG/WebP). Optional — no longer required before /complete.
Lists the booking's evidence photos, oldest-first.

Provider completes an IN_PROGRESS booking → COMPLETED. No OTP is required (the parent's code gates only start-job/verify). Evidence photos are optional. The body is OPTIONAL: nextConsultationDate (yyyy-MM-dd) proposes the pet's next visit — stored on the pet as one entry per provider type (type derived from the booking's category: PetGroomer → Groomer, Vet → Vet, PetTrainer → Trainer) and returned on the parent host's pet reads as nextConsultations[]. The optional `prescription` block { prescriptionText?, isPetVaccinated, vaccinations[] } records the visit prescription — VET BOOKINGS ONLY (400 PrescriptionNotVetBooking otherwise); it's the same payload as POST .../prescription and is surfaced on the booking-detail read's `prescription` section. Send an empty body to complete without either. 400 NextConsultationNotSupported (PetSitter/AdoptionSale booking) | NextConsultationRequiresPet (Custom walk-in, no linked pet) | InvalidNextConsultationDate (past date).

The parent has paid the provider → PAID (the last stage; only from COMPLETED). Writes a Booking.BookingPayments ledger row { Amount, PawfrontFee, PaymentMethod, ... } — Amount is computed server-side from the booking's PRICE-LOCKED total (the unit rate snapshotted at booking time, so a later price change by the provider never changes it), PawfrontFee is the platform commission on it. paymentMethod is Cash or Digital. App bookings only (Custom walk-ins are off-platform). PAID is terminal and still holds the slot / counts as a completed booking. 400 InvalidRequest (no method) | UnsupportedPaymentMethod | PaymentNotAppBooking (Custom walk-in); 403 Forbidden; 404 BookingNotFound; 409 BookingNotPayable (not COMPLETED) | BookingAlreadyPaid | BookingNotPriceable.

Records/edits the vet's per-visit prescription for a booking (upsert), independent of ending the job. VET bookings only, the booking's provider only, only once the job is IN_PROGRESS or COMPLETED. Returns the saved { prescriptionText, isPetVaccinated, vaccinations, nextConsultationDate } block — nextConsultationDate is the pet's rolling Vet follow-up (Parent.PetNextConsultations), set via /complete, joined here (null when none). The block is surfaced on the booking-detail read (GET /bookings/{id} and the parent host's GET /pet-parents/{id}/bookings/{id}) under `prescription`, null until recorded. 404 BookingNotFound; 403 Forbidden (not this provider's booking); 400 PrescriptionNotVetBooking (not a Vet booking); 409 PrescriptionNotAllowed (job not started/completed).
Provider cancels the booking → PROVIDER_CANCELLED.

Provider reports the parent (pet) never showed up → PARENT_NO_SHOW (terminal, frees the slot). Allowed only from a confirmed-equivalent state and only 30+ minutes after the booking's scheduled start (BookingDate + StartTime, UTC). 409 NoShowTooEarly before the grace window elapses; 409 BookingNotStartable from the wrong state (e.g. JOB_STARTED — the job already began).

item.name: POST request modification (provider) — stage date/time change

request.description: Provider proposes a new date/time (editing is limited to the schedule). Stages the proposal and flips the booking to MODIFICATION_REQUEST_BY_PROVIDER; the parent sees it on their booking read and accepts/declines. 409 ModificationAlreadyPending if one is already open.

item.name: POST accept modification (provider) — respond to a parent's proposal

request.description: Provider accepts the parent's staged modification → PROVIDER_ACCEPTED_MODIFICATION; the proposed date/time is applied to the booking and the staging row is removed. 409 CapacityExceeded if the new window is full; 409 NoPendingModification if nothing is staged for the provider to answer.
Provider declines the parent's staged modification → PROVIDER_DECLINED_MODIFICATION; the booking keeps its original details and the staging row is removed.

item.name: 6b. Night-Stay Bookings (provider management)
item.description: Provider-side management of multi-night boarding bookings. The booking itself is created on the parent host; set {{nightStayBookingId}} to one of the provider's stays. Same job lifecycle as single-day bookings (accept/decline/start-job + start-OTP verify/complete/cancel/modifications, evidence optional) but modifications propose a check-in/check-out date range.

request.description: All of the provider's night-stay bookings (optional ?date=YYYY-MM-DD).

Sectioned detail (mirrors the single-day booking detail): { bookingDetails (incl. jobId, checkIn/out, nights, dropOff/pickUp, serviceLocation, jobNotes), parentDetails (incl. the parent's address: addressLine, city, zipCode, latitude, longitude), petDetails (FULL medical snapshot: breed, vaccinationStatus, vaccinationType, vaccinationDose, prescription, sterilizationStatus, medicalHistory, temperament), providerDetails (providerId, providerName, mobile, gender, providerPhotoUrl (null), plus the provider's business address/city/zip from the Cosmos service doc — added so the client needn't call GET /providers/{id} just for the address), paymentDetails (pricePerNight, totalAmount, pawfrontFee), cancellationPolicy, location ({ locationType, addressLine, city, zipCode, latitude, longitude }), startOtp (null on provider), pendingModification (staged check-in/check-out proposal) }.

SNAPSHOTS (2026-07-24): `paymentDetails.pricePerNight`, `cancellationPolicy.minimumHoursBeforeCancellation` and the `location` address are read from values FROZEN onto the stay at creation, so editing your rate, cancellation policy, or business address never changes stays that already exist. Stays created before this shipped fall back to live resolution.

No body. Only on the stay's check-in (drop-off) day, and only while the provider is inside their own weekly working hours (today, UTC). 409 BookingNotOnServiceDate | OutsideWorkingHours | BookingNotStartable.
Provider enters the start-code the parent showed → IN_PROGRESS. 6 wrong attempts cancel the job (409 OtpAttemptsExceeded). 400 InvalidStartOtp; 409 StartOtpExpired | BookingNotStartable.

Provider completes an IN_PROGRESS stay → COMPLETED. No OTP and no body required. Evidence photos are optional. (No nextConsultationDate here — night-stay is PetSitter-only, which has no consultation concept.)

The parent has paid the provider → PAID (only from COMPLETED). Writes a Booking.BookingPayments ledger row (BookingType 'NightStay') — Amount is the stay's PRICE-LOCKED total (per-night rate snapshotted at booking time × nights). paymentMethod is Cash or Digital. Terminal; still counts as a completed booking. 400 InvalidRequest | UnsupportedPaymentMethod; 403 Forbidden; 404 NightStayBookingNotFound; 409 BookingNotPayable | BookingAlreadyPaid | BookingNotPriceable.

Provider reports the parent (pet) never showed up for the stay → PARENT_NO_SHOW (terminal, frees the remaining per-night capacity). Allowed only from a confirmed-equivalent state and only 30+ minutes after CheckInDate + DropOffTime (UTC). 409 NoShowTooEarly before the grace window elapses; 409 BookingNotStartable from the wrong state.

item.name: POST request modification (provider) — propose new date range

request.description: checkOutDate is the pickup day, NOT a stayed night. → MODIFICATION_REQUEST_BY_PROVIDER.

request.description: Full-replace edit of a provider-organised event — every field editable (same body shape as create). 404 EventNotFound when the event isn't found or isn't owned by this provider; 400 InvalidRequest on validation. Reconciles the Cosmos physical doc (upsert when physical; deletes the old doc when the event becomes Online or its category changes). Editing a paid event to free drops its payout methods. Returns the full detail (incl. bookings, paymentOptions, attendees). Payout methods themselves are set via the dedicated payout-methods endpoint, not this edit.

Partial edit — send ONLY the fields you want to change; everything else stays as-is. Each field is optional; an OMITTED field is left unchanged, while an explicit null CLEARS it (e.g. `"bannerImageUrl": null`). The merged event is then validated like a full edit, so cross-field rules still apply (flipping `eventType` to Physical needs a `physical` block; flipping `isPaid` to true needs a `price`). 404 EventNotFound (not found / not owned); 400 InvalidRequest. Returns the full detail (incl. bookings, paymentOptions, attendees).

item.name: 7b. Event Ticket Bookings
item.description:
Ticket purchases for an event. **Anyone** signed in can buy tickets for any names — attendee names are free text and not validated against the database. The booking is created with `PaymentStatus = Pending`; flip it to `Paid` (or `Failed`) via the gateway callback request.

`paymentMethod` ∈ {CreditCard, Twint, Cash, Free} — Cash is collected in person, Free is for no-charge bookings (validated in EventBookingService + the CK_EventBookings_PaymentMethod CHECK; same set on both hosts).

**Physical** events accept any number of tickets per booking and are capacity-gated (concurrent buyers serialise inside `Event.CreateEventBooking`; the (N+1)-th seat returns 409 EventSoldOut). **Online** events accept exactly ONE ticket per booking — more than one attendee name returns 400 OnlineEventSingleTicket, and there is no capacity limit.

item.name: POST create event booking (Credit Card, 4 tickets)

request.description:
Creates one booking row + 4 ticket rows in a single race-safe transaction. The booking comes back with `paymentStatus: "Pending"` and the `tickets` array carries one entry per attendee (TicketNumber 1..N).

Response → sets `eventBookingId` collection variable for downstream requests.
Returns the booking envelope + a `tickets` array with one entry per attendee. If 4 tickets were bought, 4 entries come back here.

Soft-cancels the caller's own booking. Authorised by your Firebase **email claim** matched against the booking's bookerEmail — so this only succeeds if you booked with the email on your token (the sample bookings above use other emails, so they would return 404 here). Flips Status → Cancelled and frees the seat capacity automatically; returns the cancelled booking + tickets. 403 EmailClaimMissing; 404 EventBookingNotFound (unknown id OR not yours); 409 EventBookingAlreadyCancelled.

Simulates the external gateway callback. Flips `PaymentStatus` to `Paid` and records the gateway reference. Idempotent for redelivery of the same (status, reference) pair; a different reference for an already-confirmed booking returns 409 PaymentAlreadyConfirmed.

item.name: 7c. Event Engagement & Organiser Dashboard
item.description:
Two halves of the same dashboard story:

**Public engagement counters** (POST views/shares/inquiries) — anyone signed in can call these from the event detail screen. Each request bumps a single counter on `Event.Events` atomically and returns the updated `{ viewCount, shareCount, inquiryCount }`. Inquiries are a counter only — there is no inquiry content stored today.

**Organiser-only reads** (GET attendees + metrics) — URL-scoped under `/providers/{providerId}/events/{eventId}`. The server verifies the event belongs to that provider; if not it returns 404 EventNotFound (we don't distinguish 'doesn't exist' vs 'not yours' to avoid leaking existence).

request.description: Atomic +1 on `Event.Events.ViewCount`. Call from the mobile event-detail screen. Returns the new `{ viewCount, shareCount, inquiryCount }`.

One row per ticket. Joins booking + ticket; excludes Cancelled bookings; surfaces `paymentStatus` per row so the organiser can chase Pending/Failed payments.

404 EventNotFound if `eventId` doesn't belong to `providerId`.

Returns `{ views, shares, inquiries, confirmedAttendees, earnings }`. `confirmedAttendees` and `earnings` are computed live from confirmed-Paid bookings; the three engagement counters are read from `Event.Events`.

404 EventNotFound if `eventId` doesn't belong to `providerId`.

item.name: POST fetch blob image by URL

request.description:
Universal image fetcher for the Flutter app. Accepts any blob URL that lives under the configured provider-images container and streams the raw image bytes back with the original Content-Type (image/jpeg, image/png, …).

**Response is binary** (not the JSON envelope) — Postman shows it under the response **Preview** tab. Errors still use the envelope:
- 400 InvalidRequest — bad URL, wrong host, or URL not in our container (SSRF guard).
- 404 BlobNotFound — blob does not exist.

Set the `blobUrl` collection variable to the URL returned by any of the upload endpoints (profile/service/event banner).
